1. Ticket Closure Procedure: - Ensure ticket resolution meets customer expectations and fulfills their requested action. - Notify customer of resolution and confirm understanding. - If resolution is not met, escalate to appropriate team lead for further assistance. - Close the ticket with appropriate status (resolved or escalated). - Document lessons learned in knowledge base for future reference.

1. Ticket Resolution Procedure: - Assess ticket severity and response time SLAs. - Attempt to resolve issue with available resources and expertise. - If resolution unsuccessful, escalate to the appropriate team or manager. - Communicate updates and solutions clearly to customer. - Once issue is resolved, close the ticket. - Document all actions taken for future reference.

Upon evaluating a ticket: 1. Assess issue severity and determine if it can be resolved immediately. 2. If the issue is critical, escalate to team leads for immediate attention. 3. For non-critical issues, implement necessary solutions and test for functionality. 4. Communicate resolution steps and outcomes to ticket requester. 5. Close ticket upon confirmation of successful resolution from requester. 6. Document lessons learned for future reference and potential improvements.

Upon assessing the ticket: 1. If resolution is achievable and immediate user feedback is obtained, mark the ticket as resolved. 2. If resolution requires further investigation or escalation to another team, update the ticket status accordingly and provide an estimated time for resolution. 3. If the issue persists beyond the SLA (Service Level Agreement), escalate it to management and notify the user of the ongoing issue and the escalation process. 4. Upon completion of the task, ensure to document all actions taken within the ticket for future reference.

On-call Engineer Ticket Resolution Guidelines: 1. Assess ticket urgency and priority upon arrival. 2. Investigate issue thoroughly, following standard troubleshooting procedures. 3. If resolved, update ticket status to 'Resolved' and notify customer. 4. If unable to resolve, document steps taken and update ticket status to 'On Hold'. 5. If escalation necessary, assign ticket to appropriate team lead and update customer. 6. Monitor ticket until resolution or further instruction.

On-call Engineer Guide: Ticket Resolution 1. Evaluate ticket urgency and impact. 2. Prioritize critical tickets first. 3. Investigate issue thoroughly. 4. Attempt to reproduce the problem. 5. Identify root cause and implement solution. 6. Test the fix to ensure no secondary issues. 7. Update ticket with resolution, steps taken, and any relevant findings. 8. Close the ticket only after confirming its successful resolution. 9. Escalate unresolved tickets to appropriate team members or management.

On-Call Engineer Ticket Resolution Guide: 1. Evaluate ticket urgency and impact. 2. Identify root cause and apply appropriate solution. 3. Test resolution thoroughly to ensure stability. 4. If unable to resolve, escalate the ticket to management or senior engineers.

Investigate issues: Gather logs, trace errors, and diagnose problems to determine root causes. 3. Identify solutions: Implement fixes, workarounds, or deploy updates as needed. 4. Test resolution: Verify that the problem has been resolved and confirm normal service operation. 5. Close ticket: Document the steps taken, outcomes, and any relevant details in the ticket's notes. 6. Communicate status: Inform affected parties of the resolution status and expected downtime. 7. Escalate when necessary: If issues persist or exceed expertise, involve senior staff or appropriate stakeholders.
